correctness.rationale: The supplied RESULT.md exactly composes the two component gradient steps, giving T12(x)=g x+eta^2 b c and T21(x)=g x-eta^2 a c with g=(1-eta a)(1-eta b), hence X_{k+1}=g X_k+m+d S_k. For every strictly stationary fair sign process, |r_h|<=1 makes the covariance series absolutely convergent under |g|<1 and initial deterministic transients vanish. Herglotz represents the covariance by a probability spectral measure and the stable filter modulus yields the bounds with denominators (1±|g|)^2. Strict monotonicity in cos(theta) for g≠0 forces point masses at 0 or pi at equality, equivalent for ±1-valued signs to a fair fixed sign or perfect alternation, respectively. The Markov formula follows by summing rho^|i-j|; differentiating has sign(g). The exact a=2,b=1 sign switches and epoch-stability interval follow from g=(1-2eta)(1-eta). In the individually-contractive family a=N,b=c=1,eta=(2N-1)/N^2, g=−(1−1/N)^3 and direct asymptotic evaluation gives the worst/best objective ratio /N^2→2/9. Checked reconstructed source tree and complete package proofs and verified independent exact rational sample recurrences and symbolic simplifications. No finite experiment substitutes for Herglotz and the universal proof.

value.rationale: The sharp cost of temporal coupling for the same two ordinary epoch permutations is a natural optimization invariant: every coupling has identical marginal sample use yet can produce the exact opposite optimal schedule depending on the step regime. Complete equality characterization and two interior phase switches within a single fixed, individually contractive problem are mathematically substantive, as is an explicit uniformly individually stable family with risk disparity asymptotic to 2N²/9. This directly motivates caution when choosing shuffle-once versus alternating epoch ordering and provides a complete benchmark rather than an arbitrary single numerical counterexample. It is not a general SGD theorem, but an exact naturally motivated fact need not be paper-sized.
residual_risks: Practical effect depends on exact scalar quadratic model and nonmixing extreme sign schedules.
No theorem for high-dimensional, nonlinear, finite-horizon, state-feedback or nonstationary gradient scheduling.
